gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-yezidi: Noto Serif Yezidi reads like a classic serif cut from glass rods, its strokes swelling and tapering into words that sit as solid blocks. Eater snarls above it, wide-gapped and dark.
gen-eater-gf-odor-mean-chey: Odor Mean Chey brings tall, rounded lowercase with squeezed mouths on its a, e and s, a dignified text serif voice. And Eater, gaps stretched wide and thin strokes free of hairlines, gives that dignity a menacing edge.
gen-eater-gf-pt-serif-caption: Literary and tall in the lowercase, PT Serif Caption is the quiet half of this pairing, with slightly thinner joins where curves meet stems. And over a long stretch its generous height keeps each line easy to take in beside Eater's aggression.
gen-eater-gf-suez-one: Bookish and refined, Suez One is the steadier voice here, set against Eater's dark, aggressive heading with its widely spaced letters. Suez One would carry a long passage with big, open bowls and thin channels into each counter, so the page keeps its footing.
gen-eater-lora: Eater sprawls across the top with wide gaps between letters and short ascenders, a dark display face with thin strokes that never turn to hairlines. Lora follows with a broad, welcoming c and a high lowercase, and a long passage would feel bookish.
gen-eater-merriweather: Wide gaps between its letters give Eater a dark, aggressive stance, with thin strokes and moderately weighty stems. Merriweather answers with a cozy, stocky line, and that soft thick-thin difference is where the pair gets its charm.
gen-fascinate-fs-sentient: Sentient reads sophisticated and contemporary, its pinched apertures and crossbars a touch lighter than the stems, which suit modest doses of text. But Fascinate is the one that commands, with blunt weight and razor-fine thread spread across generous room.
gen-fascinate-inline-fs-sentient: Sentient reads sophisticated, with pinched apertures and a soft thick-thin difference. Fascinate Inline is the vintage showpiece, dramatic in every stroke and loosely tracked, while Sentient does its best work in brief copy.
gen-flavors-fs-gambetta: Gambetta is the bookish half of this pair. Under Flavors, with its towering x-height and diagonals as heavy as its stems, it would carry a long passage gracefully, with wide channels into each counter and weight that shifts noticeably but gently.
gen-flavors-gf-cambo: Flavors towers with an x-height like a stubby carpenter's pencil, whimsical and commanding, with no shift from heavy to light inside a stroke. Cambo would settle a long passage into a refined, bookish rhythm, its modest thick and thin steady as a lettering pen.
